core_obligations: Fix the notation that treats F_1 as a subsheaf of F_2 with quotient F_3, and G_3 as a subsheaf of G_2 with quotient G_1, and record that the commutativity of the diagrams before the lemma gives gamma_2(s tensor t) = gamma_3(s-bar tensor t) for local sections s of F_2 and t of G_3 (proof lines 5672-5686).

Choose a covering and cocycles alpha_3, beta_1 representing a_3 and b_1, lift them to cochains alpha_2, beta_2 of the middle complexes, and verify that d(alpha_2) and d(beta_2) map to zero upstairs so that alpha_1 = d(alpha_2) and beta_3 = d(beta_2) represent the boundary classes (proof lines 5689-5715).

Compute d(gamma_2(alpha_2 cup beta_2)) with the Leibniz rule and the compatibility of gamma with the boundary maps to obtain gamma_1(alpha_1 cup beta_1) + (-1)^n gamma_3(alpha_3 cup beta_3), which is precisely the asserted identity with sign (-1)^{n+1} (proof lines 5716-5731).
proof_roadmap: Set up the subsheaf and quotient notation and the resulting compatibility of the products (proof lines 5672-5686).
Lift representatives of a_3 and b_1 to the middle complexes (proof lines 5689-5715).
Evaluate the differential of the product of the two lifts and read off the sign (proof lines 5716-5730).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves with a compatible product, the lemma computes the boundary of a cup product: for a in H^n(X, F_3) and b in H^m(X, G_1) one has gamma_1(boundary(a) cup b) = (-1)^{n+1} gamma_3(a cup boundary(b)) (statement lines 5656-5669). The proof is a concrete cocycle computation: after fixing the notation that identifies F_1 as a subsheaf of F_2 with quotient F_3 and G_3 as a subsheaf of G_2 with quotient G_1 (proof lines 5672-5686), the author picks cocycles alpha_3 and beta_1 on a covering, lifts them to cochains alpha_2 and beta_2, observes that alpha_1 = d(alpha_2) and beta_3 = d(beta_2) represent the two boundary classes (proof lines 5689-5715), and then evaluates d(gamma_2(alpha_2 cup beta_2)) through a four-term chain that uses the Leibniz rule for the total complex and the compatibility of the products gamma_i with the boundary maps (proof lines 5716-5730). The claim is H2: nothing is left to the reader, but the content is bookkeeping of degrees and signs inside the total complex, and the final sign is remarked to depend on the sign conventions for the long exact sequence recorded in the author's footnote.
